source_refs.note: Chapter 6 exercise as printed (PDF 171-174, printed 168-171): 18 MCQs, 9 short and 8 long questions, each with its solution. MCQ answers follow the chapter's text; the answer key (PDF 226) covers MCQs 1-10 only, and where it differs a Book correction box follows the question.

blocks.prompt: 1. What is the main benefit of edge computing?
blocks.explanation: Edge computing processes data near its source instead of in a distant data centre, so data travels less and delay (latency) is reduced, giving real-time processing (6.6.1.1).

blocks.prompt: 2. Which cloud deployment model is characterized by resources being shared among multiple organizations with common concerns?
blocks.explanation: (Beyond the chapter.) A community cloud is shared by several organizations with common concerns, such as hospitals or government departments with the same security needs. A public cloud is open to any organization, a private cloud serves one organization and a hybrid cloud mixes public and private (6.2.3).

blocks.prompt: 3. In what way does a private cloud differ from a public cloud?

options.text: A private cloud is owned and used by multiple organizations
A private cloud offers less control over data and resources
A private cloud is dedicated to a single organization and offers more control over data and security
A private cloud is cheaper and less secure than a public cloud

blocks.explanation: A private cloud is used exclusively by one organization and is not shared (6.2.3.2), so it gives more control and security, e.g. a bank keeping sensitive customer data. Public clouds are shared, cheaper and less secure (6.2.4).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key at the end of the book (Unit 6) gives (b). A private cloud gives more control, not less, because only one organization uses it (6.2.3.2, 6.2.4); the answer is (c).

blocks.prompt: 4. What is a key advantage of using a distributed ledger in blockchain technology?

options.text: The ability to easily alter transaction histories
Enhanced transparency and security due to decentralized verification
Reduced computational power needed for maintaining the ledger

blocks.explanation: Every node keeps a copy of the ledger and transactions are verified by the network, not one authority (6.4.1.2), so everyone sees the same record (transparency) and tampering is detected (security).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key at the end of the book (Unit 6) gives (b). Easily altering transaction histories is the opposite of blockchain's immutability: once a block is added it cannot be altered (6.4.1.1). The advantage is (c).

blocks.prompt: 5. Which of the following is NOT a type of cloud service?
blocks.explanation: The chapter gives three main types of cloud services: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS (6.2.2). Blockchain as a Service is not one of them.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key at the end of the book (Unit 6) gives (b). PaaS is itself one of the three main cloud service types (6.2.2.2), so it cannot be the answer; the option that is not a type in the chapter is (d) BaaS.

blocks.prompt: 6. Which cloud deployment model combines public and private cloud features?
blocks.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines public and private clouds and lets data and applications move between them (6.2.3.3), e.g. everyday work on the public cloud and sensitive data on the private cloud.

blocks.prompt: 7. In the context of blockchain, what is the purpose of using a distributed ledger?

options.text: To allow only one central authority to manage the blockchain
To enable multiple participants to share and verify data in a secure and transparent manner
To reduce the number of participants needed to maintain the network
To keep the data hidden from all participants except the central authority

blocks.explanation: The ledger is distributed across all nodes so that everyone has the same information and helps validate transactions (6.4.1.2); it lets many participants share and verify data securely and transparently.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key at the end of the book (Unit 6) gives (c). A distributed ledger does not aim to reduce the number of participants; it is copied to every node so that all of them can share and verify the data (6.4.1.2). The answer is (b).

blocks.prompt: 8. Which type of cloud service provides a platform allowing customers to develop, run, and manage applications without dealing with the underlying infrastructure?
blocks.explanation: PaaS offers a complete development and deployment environment (servers, storage, networking, middleware and tools), so developers focus on coding without managing hardware and software layers (6.2.2.2), e.g. Google App Engine.

blocks.prompt: 9. Which service model allows developers to build and deploy applications without managing servers?
blocks.explanation: Serverless architectures let developers build and deploy applications without managing servers; the cloud provider allocates resources automatically (6.6.1.2), e.g. AWS Lambda.

blocks.prompt: 10. What does Blockchain 2.0 introduce beyond basic cryptocurrency applications?
blocks.explanation: Blockchain 2.0 goes beyond cryptocurrency with smart contracts, decentralized applications (dApps) and enhanced scalability (6.6.2.1).

blocks.prompt: 11. What is a primary advantage of serverless architectures?
blocks.explanation: In a serverless model developers pay only for the computing resources they actually use and do not run their own servers (6.6.1.2), which saves cost. The other options are the opposite of serverless (it scales automatically).

blocks.prompt: 12. How does integrating AI with blockchain benefit data management?
blocks.explanation: Combining AI and blockchain enhances data security and transparency: AI analyses data stored on the blockchain while the blockchain keeps it tamper-proof (6.6.2.2).

blocks.prompt: 13. Which of the following best describes immutability in blockchain?

options.text: The ability to modify records with administrator privileges
The feature that allows data to be changed only under specific conditions
The characteristic of data being unalterable once added to the blockchain
The capability to remove data from the blockchain when no longer needed

blocks.explanation: Immutability means that once a block is added to the blockchain it cannot be altered or deleted, so the transaction history is permanent and tamper-proof (6.4.1.1).

blocks.prompt: 14. Which of the following is an example of edge computing in use?
blocks.explanation: In autonomous vehicles, data from sensors and cameras is processed locally in the vehicle, enabling quick responses to road conditions (6.6.1.1). The other options rely on central servers.

blocks.prompt: 15. What is one of the environmental concerns related to blockchain technology?
blocks.explanation: (Beyond the chapter.) Blockchains that use Proof of Work (6.4.1.1), such as Bitcoin, make many computers solve hard puzzles to add blocks, which uses a very large amount of electricity. High energy consumption is therefore an environmental concern.

blocks.prompt: 16. What is the primary function of a Peer-to-Peer (P2P) network in blockchain technology?

options.text: To increase the speed of transactions
To allow central authorities to control the network
To enable direct data sharing between nodes without a central server
To reduce the need for encryption in the network

blocks.explanation: In a P2P network the nodes communicate and share resources directly with each other without a central server, and each node acts as both client and server (6.4.1.3).

blocks.prompt: 17. Which technology benefits from processing data at the "edge" of the network?
blocks.explanation: Edge computing processes data at the "edge" of the network, near the data source, instead of relying only on centralized data centres (6.6.1.1).

blocks.prompt: 18. What is a smart contract in the context of Blockchain 2.0?

options.text: A self-executing contract with terms directly written into code
A contract managed by a third party

blocks.explanation: Smart contracts are self-executing contracts with the terms of the agreement directly written into code; they execute automatically when predefined conditions are met, without intermediaries (6.6.2.1).

blocks.prompt: 1. Analyze the role of Peer-to-Peer Networks in Blockchain. How do they function and why are they essential?
blocks.explanation:
In a P2P network, computers (nodes) communicate directly without a central server; each node is both client and server.
In blockchain, every node keeps a copy of the ledger, passes on new transactions and blocks, and validates them by consensus.
It is essential because it makes blockchain decentralized with no single point of failure, and tampering is easy to detect.

blocks.prompt: 2. Describe the concept of immutability in blockchain. Why is it a critical feature?
blocks.explanation:
Immutability: once a block is added to the blockchain, it cannot be changed or deleted.
Each block holds the previous block's hash, so changing a block breaks the chain, and the other nodes' copies reject it.
It is critical because it gives a permanent, tamper-proof record that builds trust and prevents fraud.

blocks.prompt: 3. What is edge computing and how does it benefit data processing?
blocks.explanation:
Edge computing processes data near where it is produced (the edge of the network) instead of only in distant data centres.
Benefits: lower latency, real-time processing and faster decisions, and less data sent over the network.
Example: autonomous vehicles process sensor data inside the car.

blocks.prompt: 4. Describe the concept of serverless architectures.
blocks.explanation:
In a serverless architecture, developers build and run applications without managing servers.
The cloud provider runs the servers and allocates resources automatically; the application scales with demand.
Developers pay only for the resources used, e.g. AWS Lambda.

blocks.prompt: 5. What are smart contracts in Blockchain 2.0?
blocks.explanation:
Smart contracts are self-executing contracts whose terms are written in code and run on the blockchain.
They execute automatically when the conditions are met, removing intermediaries and reducing fraud.
Example: an insurance contract pays automatically if a flight is delayed.

blocks.prompt: 6. How does integrating blockchain with IoT improve supply chain management?
blocks.explanation:
IoT sensors record a product's location, temperature and time at every stage of the supply chain.
Blockchain stores these records in a tamper-proof ledger that everyone in the chain shares.
So the product can be traced, its authenticity verified, and fraud and errors reduced.

blocks.prompt: 7. What advantages do serverless architectures offer to developers?
blocks.explanation:
No server management: no setting up, updating or maintaining servers.
Developers focus on writing code and features.
Automatic scaling with demand, and they pay only for what is used (e.g. AWS Lambda).

blocks.prompt: 8. How does edge computing improve the efficiency of autonomous vehicles?
blocks.explanation:
With edge computing, sensor and camera data is processed inside the vehicle, not in a distant data centre.
This reduces latency, so braking and steering decisions are made in real time.
Faster responses to road conditions improve safety.

blocks.prompt: 9. Differentiate between Elasticity and On-Demand access in cloud computing.
blocks.explanation: On-demand access is about getting resources quickly when needed; elasticity is about the system adjusting them automatically.

rows: The system automatically increases or decreases resources with demand
The user gets computing resources instantly whenever needed
About adjusting resources automatically
About getting resources quickly
Example: a store's servers grow during an Eid sale
Example: renting extra storage for a project

blocks.prompt: 1. Explain the structure of a distributed ledger and evaluate the rationale behind its decentralization.
blocks.explanation:
A distributed ledger is a digital record of all transactions that is copied and shared across all the nodes of a network, so that everyone has the same information (6.4.1.2).
Structure:
1. Transactions: each transaction is an individual entry recording a transfer of assets or information between participants.
2. Blocks: transactions are bundled into blocks. Each block contains its own unique identifier (hash), a reference to the previous block (parent hash) and a list of transactions, with a timestamp (Figure 6.2).
3. Chain: because each block points to the one before it, the blocks form a chain in order, back to the first block (Block 0).
4. Nodes: every computer (node) on the peer-to-peer network keeps a full copy of the chain and helps validate transactions and blocks.
5. Protocol and consensus: the blockchain protocol sets the rules for validating transactions and adding blocks; consensus mechanisms such as Proof of Work and Proof of Stake let the nodes agree before a new block is added.
Rationale for decentralization (evaluation):
- No central authority is needed: trust comes from the network's agreement, not from one bank or company.
- No single point of failure: if some nodes fail or are attacked, the others keep the ledger working, which enhances security.
- Tamper resistance: changing a record would require changing it on most copies and breaking the hash links, so fraud is easily detected (immutability).
- Transparency and fairness: everyone sees the same record, and changes are made only when the majority agree.
- Limitations: keeping many copies and reaching consensus needs more computing power and energy and can be slower than a central database; but for money, contracts, voting and supply chains, security and trust are worth this cost.
Conclusion: decentralization makes the ledger secure, transparent and trustworthy without relying on any one party.

blocks.prompt: 4. Discuss the advancements and benefits of edge computing in modern technology.
blocks.explanation:
Edge computing is an advancement in cloud computing that brings processing power closer to the data sources. Instead of sending all data to centralized data centres, data is processed at the "edge" of the network, near where it is produced (6.6.1.1).
Advancements:
- Processing moves from distant data centres to devices and local systems near the data (vehicles, sensors, machines).
- It works together with the cloud: urgent processing happens at the edge, while the cloud handles storage and large-scale analysis.
Benefits:
1. Reduced latency: data travels a shorter distance, so responses are faster.
2. Real-time processing and faster decision-making.
3. Improved efficiency: less data needs to be sent over the network (saving bandwidth).
4. Greater safety where split-second reactions matter.
Applications in modern technology:
- Autonomous vehicles: sensor and camera data is processed in the vehicle for quick responses to road conditions.
- Smart cities: e.g. traffic signals reacting to live traffic.
- Healthcare monitoring: patient data analysed immediately at the device.
- Industrial automation: machines detect and respond to problems on the spot.
Conclusion: edge computing, along with serverless architectures, is making cloud computing faster, more efficient and more scalable (6.6).

blocks.prompt: 5. Explain the concept of serverless architectures and their impact on application development.
blocks.explanation:
Concept: serverless architectures allow developers to build and deploy applications without managing servers (6.6.1.2). The servers still exist, but the cloud provider runs them and automatically allocates resources as needed; developers pay only for the actual usage of computing resources.
How it works:
- The developer writes code (usually small functions) and uploads it to the provider.
- The provider runs the code whenever it is needed, adding or removing resources automatically.
- Example: AWS Lambda lets developers run code without provisioning or managing servers.
Impact on application development:
1. Focus on code: developers spend time writing code and building features rather than managing infrastructure.
2. Reduced operational complexity: no installing, updating or maintaining servers.
3. Automatic scalability: the application scales with demand, from a few users to very many.
4. Cost savings: pay only for the resources used, nothing for idle servers.
5. Faster development: applications are built, tested and deployed more quickly.
Conclusion: serverless architectures make cloud application development simpler, cheaper and more scalable.

blocks.prompt: 6. Describe Blockchain 2.0 and its advanced features.
blocks.explanation:
Blockchain 2.0 refers to innovations in blockchain technology that introduce advanced features and capabilities beyond basic cryptocurrency applications (6.6.2.1). Blockchain 1.0 was mainly digital money (e.g. Bitcoin); Blockchain 2.0 runs programs on the blockchain.
Advanced features:
1. Smart contracts
- Self-executing contracts with the terms of the agreement written directly into code.
- They automatically execute and enforce the terms when predefined conditions are met, reducing the need for intermediaries.
- Example: in real estate, when payment and ownership verification are complete, the contract transfers ownership to the buyer and funds to the seller automatically. An insurance contract can pay out automatically if a flight is delayed (6.4.3.2).
2. Decentralized applications (dApps)
- Applications that run on a blockchain network instead of one company's server; platforms like Ethereum let developers build them with smart contracts.
3. Enhanced scalability
- The ability to handle more transactions and users efficiently.
Benefits: transparency (everyone can see the contract terms), security (execution is guaranteed by the blockchain), and fewer errors and less fraud.
Uses: finance, supply-chain management, real estate and insurance.
Challenges: smart contract code must be error-free, and legal systems are needed to resolve disputes.

blocks.prompt: 7. How does integrating blockchain with AI and IoT create new opportunities and synergies?
blocks.explanation:
Blockchain is being integrated with other emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. Each technology covers the others' weaknesses, which creates synergies (combined benefits greater than each alone) and new opportunities for innovation (6.6.2.2).
1. AI and blockchain
- Blockchain keeps data secure, transparent and tamper-proof; AI analyses this trusted data to give insights.
- Together they enhance data security and transparency, ensure data integrity and provide insights without compromising privacy.
- Example: in supply-chain management, AI predicts demand and optimizes logistics using secure data stored on the blockchain, giving efficient and reliable supply chains.
2. IoT and blockchain
- IoT devices (sensors, smart machines) collect data; blockchain gives a decentralized, tamper-proof ledger for recording it.
- This ensures secure and transparent data exchange between devices and enhances trust and security.
- Example: in agriculture, IoT sensors monitor soil conditions and crop health and record the data on the blockchain; authentic data helps farmers make informed decisions and improve crop yields.
3. AI, IoT and blockchain together
- IoT collects data, blockchain secures it, and AI turns it into predictions and automatic decisions (smart contracts can then act on them).
- Opportunities: tracking product origin from supplier to customer, smart agriculture, healthcare records, smart cities and secure certificate verification.
Conclusion: the integration expands blockchain's applications beyond cryptocurrency and enhances the capabilities of all the technologies involved.

blocks.prompt: 8. Describe “Cloud Deployment Models” with examples.
blocks.explanation:
Cloud deployment models define how cloud services are made available and used. Each model offers different levels of control, security and flexibility (6.2.3).
1. Public cloud
- A cloud service offered over the internet and shared among multiple organizations, managed by a third-party cloud service provider.
- Example: Amazon Web Services (AWS); businesses of all sizes use it for virtual servers and storage without managing physical hardware.
- Cost-effective but less secure.
2. Private cloud
- A cloud environment used exclusively by one organization, hosted on-premises or by a third party, not shared with others.
- Example: a large bank uses a private cloud in its own data centre to handle sensitive customer data securely.
- More secure but expensive.
3. Hybrid cloud
- Combines public and private clouds, allowing data and applications to be shared between them.
- Example: a company uses the public cloud for everyday operations and a private cloud for sensitive data; in busy periods, less sensitive work is moved to the public cloud.
- Offers flexibility and control.
4. Multi-cloud
- Uses multiple cloud services from different providers to avoid dependency on a single provider.
- Example: Google Cloud Platform for data analytics, Microsoft Azure for enterprise applications and AWS for backup and disaster recovery.
- Provides resilience: if one provider has problems, the others keep working.
(Community cloud, shared by organizations with common concerns, is another model; it is not described in the chapter.)
